Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-slack-medium-0078", "row_sha256": "524e62e5e5885fcf8c19ec24d6369b25f7b7a2808c1325760d37643cfa91a70e", "mode": "/slack", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Fix grammar, punctuation, and shorthand with minimal edits. Keep casual tone, contractions, emoji, and the original request. Return correct text unchanged.", "input": "hey folks, i pulled the latest community survey export from the shared drive this morning. could someone give the csv a quick check b4 we send the summary to the neighborhood group? the rows are grouped by block, and the response totals are in the last col. i noticed two entries have the same street name but different apartment numbers, so pls leave both in place unless you can confirm they're duplicates. don't change the wording of the free-text comments; a couple mention the Saturday cleanup and library hours, and we need those left as respondents wrote them. for the photo field, do not publish photos. it should stay out of anything shared with the group, but the export itself can remain in the team folder. we can share the anonymized totals in the summary. if the chart's easy to refresh, could you update it using the same block labels as last month? no need to make a new design, just check the labels and send me a note if any totals don't match the sheet. also, the survey covers responses from May 1 through May 14, and the summary is due Thursday afternoon. thanks!", "output": "Hey folks, I pulled the latest community survey export from the shared drive this morning. Could someone give the CSV a quick check before we send the summary to the neighborhood group? The rows are grouped by block, and the response totals are in the last column. I noticed two entries have the same street name but different apartment numbers, so please leave both in place unless you can confirm they're duplicates. Don't change the wording of the free-text comments; a couple mention the Saturday cleanup and library hours, and we need those left as respondents wrote them. For the photo field, do not publish photos. It should stay out of anything shared with the group, but the export itself can remain in the team folder. We can share the anonymized totals in the summary. If the chart's easy to refresh, could you update it using the same block labels as last month? No need to make a new design; just check the labels and send me a note if any totals don't match the sheet. Also, the survey covers responses from May 1 through May 14, and the summary is due Thursday afternoon. Thanks!"}]
